agent: agent

# Rewrite a course as a first-principles practical guide

Target: course `${input:course:course slug under content/, e.g. llm-serving}`, sections `${input:sections:all, or a range like 01-08}`.

Rewrite the target sections in place so every idea is built from basics to practice:
**intuition → math → worked numbers → picture → runnable code → practical rules**. Readers are working
engineers: precise, concrete, zero filler.

## 1. Orient before writing

1. Start the dev server if it isn't running: `npm run dev -- -p 3123` (check `lsof -i :3123` first; never start a second one).
2. Read `content/<course>/course.json` and every section in the course (not just the targets) to learn its
   scope, terminology, symbols and existing numbers.
3. Pick 1–2 **running examples** the whole course reuses (a concrete system with real-looking parameters,
   e.g. a model size, a traffic level, a cost). Prefer ones already in the course. Write them down and keep
   every section consistent with them.
4. Read 2–3 already-rewritten sections as the style reference:
   `content/practical-slm-decision-models/04-decision-theory.md` (deep theory),
   `content/slm-decision-models/16-finance.md` (applied handbook).
5. If another course covers the same derivation, summarise it in 2–4 sentences and link to it instead of repeating.

## 2. Section template (adapt, don't pad)

1. Frontmatter — keep filename, `section`, `order`. Update `abstract` (1–2 sentences), `time` (~200 words/min
   plus code), `kicker`, and 3–5 concrete `outcomes` ("Compute…", "Decide…", "Size…").
2. Opening paragraph — the concrete problem this section solves, in a specific scenario.
3. `:::key[First principle]` — the core idea in 1–3 sentences.
4. Numbered `## N.1 …` subsections. Per idea: intuition → KaTeX math → `:::example` with real numbers →
   `:::chart` when a quantity varies → code when it helps.
5. Practical guidance — decision tables, rules of thumb **with numbers**, checklists, `:::warn` failure modes.
6. `## N.x Check yourself` — 3–5 `:::qa[...]` items with worked answers.
7. Close with a one-line link to the next section (`/c/<course>/<file-slug>`; verify the slug exists).

Length: theory sections ~250–450 lines, applied sections ~150–300. Cut anything that doesn't teach.

## 3. Truthfulness rules (non-negotiable)

- **Every number is computed or labelled.** Compute with a Python script you actually run (stdlib, numpy,
  scikit-learn) and paste the results. Assumptions (prices, hardware rates, latencies) are labelled
  "illustrative" or derived from first principles with the arithmetic shown
  (e.g. decode time ≈ bytes read per token ÷ memory bandwidth).
- Don't invent benchmarks, papers, citations or product claims. Well-known facts are fine; when unsure,
  describe the method instead of quoting a number. Remove existing numbers you can't reproduce.
- ```` ```python run ```` blocks must run as-is (fixed seeds, < ~70 lines). Put the real stdout in an
  ```` ```output ```` block right after. Non-runnable sketches use plain ```` ```python ````.
- No secrets or credentials in examples; follow security best practice (non-root containers, pinned versions).

## 4. Renderer features (use them)

GFM: headings, tables (`|---:|` alignment), task lists, links, images, blockquotes.

**Math (KaTeX):** inline `$…$` or `\( … \)`; display `$$ … $$` or `\[ … \]` on their own lines
(`aligned`, `\text{}`, `\frac`, `\sum` all work). `$` followed by a digit never opens math, so `$500` is
safe; never write `$` + letter for money. Inline math that *starts* with a digit must use `\( … \)`.

**Callouts** — close with a bare `:::`; they nest and may contain code, math, tables:

```
:::key[First principle]          :::example[Worked example · …]   :::tip[…]
:::warn[…]                       :::note[…]                        :::pull
:::details[Show the derivation]  :::qa[Question?]
```

**Charts** — CSV body, header row first, first column is x (numeric → linear axis, text → categories):

```
:::chart[Caption]{type="line" x="x title" y="y title" marks="0.833:threshold"}
p, approve, decline
0, 120000, 0
1, 0, 24000
:::
```

Options: `type` line|area|scatter|bar; `stacked`, `xlog`, `ylog`, `diag`, `points`, `labels` (`"true"`);
`xmin xmax ymin ymax`; `xfmt`/`yfmt` pct|int|dec1|dec2|dec3; `prefix`, `unit`, `xprefix`, `xunit`;
`marks="x:label;…"` (numeric x only), `hmarks="y:label"`, `band="x0:x1:label"`, `dash="series,…"`, `note`,
`height`. ≤ 6 series, ≤ ~40 rows, data generated by Python. Quote cells containing commas or use `|`.
**Never use raw `<svg>`** — convert existing inline SVG charts to `:::chart`.

**Diagrams:** ```` ```mermaid ```` (or `:::mermaid[Caption]`): flowchart, sequenceDiagram,
stateDiagram-v2; ≤ ~10 nodes; no double quotes inside labels.

**Exercises:** `:::exercise[Title]{id="…" …}` with ids `scorecard`, `budget`, `checklist`, `threshold`
(see README → Exercises). Only add a new exercise component if the user asks.

## 5. Work plan

- More than ~4 target sections: split into batches of 3–4 and hand each batch to a subagent with this
  prompt's rules, the running examples, and the exact file list. Subagents edit only their files and put
  scratch scripts under `/tmp/<batch>/`. Run batches in parallel when independent.
- Don't touch app code, other courses, package files or git while rewriting.

## 6. Verify (required, per file)

1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3123/c/<course>/<slug>` → `200`
2. `curl -s http://localhost:3123/c/<course>/<slug> | grep -c katex-error` → `0`
3. No raw directives in the HTML: `grep -o ':::[a-z]\+'` → nothing.
4. Every `:::` directive and code fence is closed; every `python run` block re-run and its output matches.
5. Every internal link resolves to an existing file.
6. Spot-check a few pages in the browser: Mermaid renders an SVG, charts draw, no console errors.

## 7. Finish

Report per file: line count, charts, runnable blocks, verification results, and every number labelled
illustrative. Then offer to commit in logical steps (e.g. `docs(content): rewrite <course> sections 1–10`)
using the repo's local git identity. Don't push unless asked.
